The `CholeskyDecompositionImpl` class provides a constructor that takes a `RealMatrix` as input and performs Cholesky decomposition on the matrix. The `multiply` method in the `DenseRealMatrix` class is used to perform matrix multiplication.

In the failing test case `testNotPositiveDefinite`, a `RealMatrix` with the following values is created:

```
{ 14, 11, 13, 15, 24 },
{ 11, 34, 13, 8,  25 },
{ 13, 13, 14, 15, 21 },
{ 15, 8,  15, 18, 23 },
{ 24, 25, 21, 23, 45 }
```

Cholesky decomposition is then performed on this matrix. Finally, the product of the lower triangular matrix (L) and its transpose (LT) is printed.

The bug report indicates a successful test with a symmetric positive definite matrix, but a failure with another matrix. The bug report is cut off but it seems to involve a matrix with negative values, which may be causing the failure in Cholesky decomposition for non-positive definite matrices.

To diagnose the issue further, we would need to investigate how the Cholesky decomposition is implemented in `CholeskyDecompositionImpl` and how matrix multiplication is done in `DenseRealMatrix`. The failure could be due to issues in the decomposition algorithm or the multiplication logic, especially when dealing with non-positive definite matrices or matrices with negative values.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
